title: How to Connect Trello to Google Calendar (3 Ways)
description: Trello's built-in calendar feed, two-way sync with Zapier/Make, and an API approach, compared for effort and freshness.
bodyHtml:
Trello cards with due dates and Google Calendar events overlap in purpose, so teams often want cards to show up on a calendar without re-entering them. The right method depends on whether one-way visibility is enough, or you need true two-way sync.

MethodSetup effortBest for
Trello Calendar Power-Up (iCal feed)LowOne-way, read-only view of card due dates
Zapier / MakeMediumTwo-way sync, creating cards from calendar events or vice versa
API integration (custom)HighConditional logic, syncing specific boards/labels only

Method 1: Trello's Calendar Power-Up

Enable the Calendar Power-Up on a board, then use "Share, print, and export" to get an iCalendar (.ics) feed URL. Add that URL in Google Calendar under "Other calendars → From URL". Cards with due dates now appear as events. This is one-way and read-only: editing the calendar event won't change the Trello card, and Google Calendar typically refreshes external feeds every few hours, so it isn't real-time.

Method 2: Zapier or Make (two-way sync)

To get real two-way sync, e.g. a new Trello card creates a Calendar event, and moving the due date updates it, use two zaps/scenarios:

  • Trigger: "Card Due Date" or "New Card" in Trello → Action: "Create Detailed Event" in Google Calendar
  • Trigger: "Event Start" changed in Google Calendar → Action: "Update Card" in Trello

This needs more setup than the Power-Up but stays live and current in both directions.

Method 3: API integration (for developers)

For syncing only specific labels/lists, or merging multiple boards into one calendar with custom event formatting, call the Trello REST API for card data and the Google Calendar API to upsert events. Useful when the no-code tools' rate limits or field-mapping options fall short.

Which to pick

Use the Power-Up feed if you just want visibility of deadlines. Use Zapier/Make once the calendar needs to be a source of truth in both directions. Go custom only for board-specific filtering or high card volume.
